value.zh: 張禕
value.en: Zhang Yi
value.literal: Zhang Yi

value.zh: 張禕，吳郡人也。
value.en: Zhang Yi came from Wu commandery.
value.literal: Zhang Yi was a man of Wu commandery.

value.zh: 少有操行。
value.en: Even young he lived upright.
value.literal: In youth he had conduct and integrity.

value.zh: 恭帝為琅邪王，以禕為郎中令。
value.en: As Prince of Langye, Emperor Gong named him palace captain.
value.literal: When Emperor Gong was Prince of Langye—appointed Yi Palace Captain.

value.zh: 及帝踐阼，劉裕以禕帝之故吏，素所親信，封藥酒一罌付禕密令鴆帝。
value.en: After Gong took the throne, Liu Yu—trusting Yi as an old aide—handed him sealed wine to poison the retired emperor.
value.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne—Liu Yu because Yi was the emperor's former clerk—long intimate—sealed a jug of poisoned wine—delivered it to Yi with secret order to poison the sovereign.

value.zh: 禕既受命而歎曰：「鴆君而求生，何面目視息世間哉，不如死也！」
value.en: Yi cried: "Murder my lord and yet seek to live—what face would I show breathing in this world—better to die!"
value.literal: Yi having received the charge sighed: "Poisoning the ruler yet seeking life—what face to breathe in this world—better to die!

value.zh: 因自飲之而死。
value.en: He swallowed the draught and died.
value.literal: Thereupon drank it himself and died.

value.zh: 嚴武，中書侍郎挺之子也。
value.en: Yan Wu was the son of Ting, who had served as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
value.literal: Yan Wu was the son of Ting, Vice Director of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 神氣雋爽，敏於聞見。
value.en: He had a keen, commanding presence and was unusually quick to grasp what he heard and saw.
value.literal: His spirit and bearing were sharp and lofty, and he was quick in what he heard and observed.

value.zh: 幼有成人之風，讀書不究精義，涉獵而已。
value.en: Even as a boy he carried himself like an adult; he read widely but never troubled to master texts in depth.
value.literal: In youth he had the manner of a grown man; in reading he did not pursue the deepest meanings but merely ranged broadly.

value.zh: 弱冠以門廕策名，隴右節度使哥舒翰奏充判官，遷侍御史。
value.en: At his coming of age he qualified through family privilege; Geshu Han, military commissioner of Longyou, had him appointed as aide on memorial and then promoted him to Attending Censor.
value.literal: Upon reaching the capping age he entered the rolls through hereditary privilege; the Longyou Military Commissioner Geshu Han memorialized to appoint him as aide, and he was promoted to Attending Censor.

value.zh: 至德初，肅宗興師靖難，大收才傑，武杖節赴行在。
value.en: Early in the Zhide reign, as Emperor Suzong mobilized to put down the rebellion and recruited talent far and wide, Wu took up his commission and hurried to the emperor's camp.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide era, when Emperor Suzong raised armies to quell the rebellion and gathered outstanding men on a large scale, Wu took the staff of office and went to the mobile court.

value.zh: 宰相房琯以武名臣之子，素重之，及是，首薦才略可稱，累遷給事中。
value.en: Chief Minister Fang Guan had always held Wu in esteem as the son of a distinguished official; now he was first to recommend him for his ability and was instrumental in promoting him repeatedly until he reached Supervising Secretary.
value.literal: The Chief Minister Fang Guan, because Wu was the son of a famous minister, had long valued him; on this occasion he was the first to recommend that his talent and strategy were commendable, and Wu was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Secretary.

value.zh: 既收長安，以武為京兆少尹、兼御史中丞，時年三十二。
value.en: Once Chang'an had been retaken, he was appointed Vice Governor of the capital district and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief at the age of thirty-two.
value.literal: After Chang'an was recovered, Wu was made Vice Governor of Jingzhao and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief; he was then thirty-two.

value.zh: 以史思明阻兵不之官，優遊京師，頗自矜大。
value.en: With Shi Siming's armies blocking the routes, he never took up his post and instead lingered in the capital, growing rather full of himself.
value.literal: Because Shi Siming obstructed the roads with his troops, he did not take up the post but idled in the capital, quite self-important.

value.zh: 出為綿州刺史，遷劍南東川節度使；
value.en: He was sent out to serve as prefect of Mianzhou and later promoted to military commissioner of eastern Jiannan.
value.literal: He went out as Prefect of Mianzhou and was transferred to Military Commissioner of Jiannan East Circuit;

value.zh: 入為太子賓客、兼御史中丞。
value.en: He was recalled to the capital as a guest of the heir apparent and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.
value.literal: He entered the capital as Guest of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief.

value.zh: 前後在蜀累年，肆誌逞欲，恣行猛政。
value.en: During his long years in Shu he gave free rein to his appetites and ruled with arbitrary severity.
value.literal: Over many years before and after in Shu he indulged his will and desires and arbitrarily carried out harsh government.

value.zh: 梓州刺史章彜初為武判官，及是小不副意，赴成都杖殺之，由是威震一方。
value.en: Zhang Yi of Zizhou had once served as his aide; when Yi displeased him even slightly, Wu summoned him to Chengdu and had him clubbed to death, and thereafter his terror held the whole region.
value.literal: Zhang Yi, Prefect of Zizhou, had first been Wu's aide; when he fell slightly short of Wu's wishes, Wu had him brought to Chengdu and beaten to death with the staff, and from this his awe filled the region.

value.zh: 蜀土頗饒珍產，武窮極奢靡，賞賜無度，或由一言賞至百萬。
value.en: Shu was rich in rare goods, and Wu spent without limit; a single pleasing word from him could bring a reward of a million cash.
value.literal: The land of Shu was quite rich in rare products; Wu pursued luxury to the extreme, his rewards without limit, and sometimes for a single remark he would grant up to a million.

value.zh: 蜀方閭裏以征斂殆至匱竭，然蕃虜亦不敢犯境。
value.en: Taxes and levies nearly beggared the countryside, yet frontier tribes likewise dared not cross his borders.
value.literal: In the villages of Shu, levies brought them nearly to exhaustion, yet the barbarians of the frontier also did not dare to violate the borders.

value.zh: 而性本狂蕩，視事多率胸臆，雖慈母言不之顧。
value.en: By nature he was headstrong and impulsive, governing mostly on whim; he would not even listen to his own mother.
value.literal: Yet his nature was fundamentally reckless; in conducting affairs he mostly followed his breast and belly, and even his loving mother's words he did not heed.

value.zh: 初為劍南節度使，舊相房琯出為管內刺史，琯於武有薦導之恩，武驕倨，見琯略無朝禮，甚為時議所貶。
value.en: When he first took command in Jiannan, his former patron Fang Guan was serving as a circuit prefect; though Guan had launched his career, Wu treated him with arrogant disrespect and scarcely a trace of formal courtesy, drawing widespread condemnation.
value.literal: When he first became Military Commissioner of Jiannan, the former Chief Minister Fang Guan went out as a prefect within the circuit; Guan had the grace of recommending and guiding Wu, but Wu was arrogant and haughty and on seeing Guan showed hardly any court etiquette, and this was much decried in contemporary opinion.

value.zh: 永泰元年四月，以疾終，時年四十。
value.en: He died of illness in the fourth month of 765, at the age of forty.
value.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongtai he died of illness; he was then forty.

value.zh: 王璵 道士李國禎附
value.en: Wang Yu — with an appended account of the Daoist Li Guozhen
value.literal: Wang Yu; appended: the Daoist Li Guozhen

value.zh: 建中初，張鎰為河中少尹。
value.en: At the beginning of the Jianzhong reign, Zhang Yi served as Vice Governor of Hezhong.
value.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Zhang Yi was Vice Governor of Hezhong.

value.zh: 鎰尋入相，二年七月，遷播給事中。
value.en: Zhang Yi soon entered the chancellorship. In the seventh month of Jianzhong 2, Guan Bo was promoted to Supervising Secretary.
value.literal: Yi soon entered the chancellorship; in the seventh month of the second year, Bo was promoted to Supervising Secretary.

value.zh: 舊例，諸司甲庫，皆是胥吏掌知，為弊頗久，播始建議並以士人知之，至今稱當。
value.en: By longstanding custom, the personnel archives of the various ministries had been managed by low-level clerks—a source of chronic abuse. Guan Bo was the first to propose placing educated officials in charge of them, a reform still praised as apt.
value.literal: By old precedent, the archives of the various offices were all managed by clerks and runners—a abuse long standing; Bo first proposed that gentlemen-scholars manage them jointly, and to this day it is called appropriate.

value.zh: 轉刑部侍郎、奉迎皇太后副使。
value.en: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and Deputy Commissioner for Welcoming the Empress Dowager.
value.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and Deputy Commissioner for Welcoming the Empress Dowager.

value.zh: 盧杞以播柔緩，冀其易制，驟稱薦之。
value.en: Lu Qi, judging Guan Bo gentle and pliable, hoped to control him easily and suddenly began praising and recommending him.
value.literal: Lu Qi, because Bo was gentle and mild, hoped he would be easy to control and abruptly praised and recommended him.

value.zh: 尋遷吏部侍郎，轉刑部尚書、知刪定。
value.en: He was soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, then transferred to Minister of Justice with charge over statutory revision.
value.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, then transferred to Minister of Justice and placed in charge of statutory revision.

value.zh: 奏上元中，詔擇古今名將十人於武成王廟配享，如文宣王廟之儀。
value.en: He reported that during the Shangyuan reign an edict had selected ten famous generals from history for companion worship in the Temple of the Martial Accomplishment King, patterned after the rites of Confucius's temple.
value.literal: He memorialized that in the Shangyuan era an edict had chosen ten famous generals from ancient and modern times for companion worship at the Temple of the Martial Accomplishment King, following the ritual of the Temple of the Literary Sage King.

value.zh: 播以「太公古稱大賢，今其下稱亞聖，於義不安。
value.en: Guan Bo argued, "The Grand Duke was called a great sage in antiquity; to designate those beneath him as 'lesser sages' is improper in principle.
value.literal: Bo argued: "The Grand Duke was anciently called a great sage; now beneath him they are called sub-sages—in propriety this is unsettling.

value.zh: 又孔子十哲，皆是當時弟子，今所擇名將，年代不同，於義既乖，於事又失。
value.en: Moreover, Confucius's Ten Worthies were all disciples of his own day. The generals now chosen belong to different ages. This violates principle and misses the point in practice as well.
value.literal: Moreover Confucius's Ten Worthies were all disciples of his own time; the famous generals now chosen belong to different ages—in principle this already conflicts, and in practice it is also wrong.

value.zh: 臣請刪去名將配享之儀及十哲之稱。」
value.en: I therefore request that the rite of companion worship for famous generals and the designation 'Ten Worthies' be abolished."
value.literal: Your subject requests deletion of the rite of companion worship for famous generals and the title of Ten Worthies.

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: The request was granted.
value.literal: This was approved.

value.zh: 潘孟陽，禮部侍郎炎之子也。
value.en: Pan Mengyang was the son of Yan, Minister of Rites.
value.literal: Pan Mengyang was the son of Yan, Vice Minister of Rites.

value.zh: 孟陽以父廕進，登博學宏辭科。
value.en: Mengyang entered service through his father's privilege and passed the Boxue Hongci examination.
value.literal: Mengyang advanced through his father's yin privilege and passed the Broad Learning and Eloquent Expression examination.

value.zh: 累遷殿中侍御史，降為司議郎。
value.en: He rose to Palace Censor, then was demoted to Secretariat Drafter.
value.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Censor, then demoted to Secretariat Drafter.

value.zh: 孟陽母，劉晏女也。
value.en: Mengyang's mother was Liu Yan's daughter.
value.literal: Mengyang's mother was a daughter of Liu Yan.

value.zh: 公卿多父友及外祖賓從，故得薦用，累至兵部郎中。
value.en: Many high officials were friends of his father or associates of his maternal grandfather, so he won recommendations and rose to bureau director in the Ministry of War.
value.literal: Many ministers and officials were his father's friends and his maternal grandfather's associates and followers, so he was recommended for appointment and rose to Bureau Director of the Ministry of War.

value.zh: 祎，字冠章，釋褐汴州從事、戶部判官，入為藍田尉、集賢校理。
value.en: Yi, styled Guanzhang, first served as staff in Bian and revenue judge, entered court as magistrate of Lantian and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
value.literal: Yi, styled Guanzhang, on leaving office served as staff in Bian Prefecture and revenue judge, entered court as magistrate of Lantian and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

value.zh: 趙隱鎮浙西，劉鄴鎮淮南，皆辟為賓佐。
value.en: When Zhao Yin governed Zhexi and Liu Ye governed Huainan, both recruited him as staff.
value.literal: When Zhao Yin governed Zhexi and Liu Ye governed Huainan, both recruited him as staff.

value.zh: 入為監察御史，遷左補闕。
value.en: He entered court as investigating censor and rose to left reminder.
value.literal: He entered court as Investigating Censor and was promoted to Left Reminder.

value.zh: 乾符中，詔入翰林為學士，累官至中書舍人。
value.en: In the Qianfu era an edict summoned him to the Hanlin Academy; he rose repeatedly to drafting attendant.
value.literal: In the Qianfu era an edict summoned him to the Hanlin Academy as academician; he rose repeatedly to Drafting Attendant.

value.zh: 黃巢犯京師，從僖宗幸蜀，拜工部侍郎，判戶部事。
value.en: When Huang Chao attacked the capital he followed Emperor Xizong to Shu and was appointed vice minister of works with charge of revenue.
value.literal: When Huang Chao attacked the capital he followed Emperor Xizong to Shu and was appointed Vice Minister of Works with charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

value.zh: 奉使江淮還，為當塗者不協，改太子賓客、左散騎常侍，轉吏部侍郎，歷刑部、兵部尚書。
value.en: Returning from a Jianghuai mission he was at odds with the man in power and was changed to crown prince's mentor and left regular attendant, then vice minister of personnel, and successively minister of justice and minister of war.
value.literal: On returning from a mission to the Jianghuai region he was at odds with the man in power and was changed to Crown Prince's Mentor and Left Regular Attendant, then Vice Minister of Personnel, and successively Minister of Justice and Minister of War.

value.zh: 從昭宗在華，為韓建所構，貶衡州司馬。
value.en: Following Emperor Zhaozong at Hua he was framed by Han Jian and demoted to vice magistrate of Heng.
value.literal: Following Emperor Zhaozong at Hua he was framed by Han Jian and demoted to Vice Magistrate of Heng Prefecture.

value.zh: 昭宗還京，征拜禮部尚書、太常卿，充禮儀使，遷兵部尚書。
value.en: When Zhaozong returned to the capital he was summoned as minister of rites and grand minister of imperial sacrifices and ritual commissioner, then promoted to minister of war.
value.literal: When Zhaozong returned to the capital he was summoned as Minister of Rites and Grand Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and made ritual commissioner, then promoted to Minister of War.

value.zh: 祎苦心為文，老而益壯。
value.en: Yi labored at writing; in old age his work grew stronger.
value.literal: Yi labored at writing; in old age his work grew stronger.

value.zh: 為刑部時，劉鄴子覃，當巢寇時避禍於金吾將軍張直方之第，被害。
value.en: When he was minister of justice, Liu Ye's son Tan, during the Huang Chao rebellion, had taken refuge in Gold Crow Guard commander Zhang Zhifang's residence and was killed.
value.literal: When he was Minister of Justice, Liu Ye's son Tan, during the Huang Chao rebellion, had taken refuge in the residence of Gold Crow Guard commander Zhang Zhifang and was killed.

value.zh: 僖宗還京，而惡覃者以托附逆黨，死不以義，下三司詳罪。
value.en: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital those who hated Tan accused him of attaching himself to rebels and dying without righteousness; the Three Offices were ordered to examine the crime.
value.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital those who hated Tan accused him of attaching himself to the rebel party and dying without righteousness; the Three Offices were ordered to examine the crime in detail.

value.zh: 祎上章申理，言覃父子並命於賊廷，豈附逆耶？
value.en: Yi submitted a memorial in his defense, saying father and son both met death in the rebel court—how could this be joining rebellion?
value.literal: Yi submitted a memorial in his defense, saying father and son both met their deaths in the rebel court—how could this be joining rebellion?

value.zh: 其家竟獲洗雪，覃亦贈官。
value.en: His family finally obtained rehabilitation and Tan was also posthumously granted office.
value.literal: His family finally obtained rehabilitation and Tan was also posthumously granted office.

value.zh: 其行義始終，皆如此類。
value.en: His righteous conduct from beginning to end was all of this kind.
value.literal: His righteous conduct from beginning to end was all of this kind.

value.zh: 英宗法天立道仁明誠敬昭文憲武至德廣孝睿皇帝，諱祁鎮，宣宗長子也。
value.en: Emperor Yingzong—honored after death as one who patterned himself on Heaven, established the Way, and united benevolence, brilliance, sincerity, reverence, literary glory, martial achievement, supreme virtue, broad filial devotion, and sagely wisdom—was named Zhu Qizhen and was the eldest son of Emperor Xuanzong.
value.literal: The Yingzong Emperor, patterning Heaven and establishing the Way, benevolent, bright, sincere, reverent, illustrious in culture, manifest in martial virtue, of utmost virtue, broadly filial, and sagely, taboo name Qizhen, was the Xuanzong Emperor's eldest son.

value.zh: 母貴妃孫氏。
value.en: His mother was Noble Consort Sun.
value.literal: His mother was Noble Consort Sun.

value.zh: 生四月，立為皇太子，遂冊貴妃為皇后。
value.en: When he was four months old he was named crown prince, and Noble Consort Sun was at once elevated to empress.
value.literal: At four months he was established Crown Prince; the noble consort was then enfeoffed as Empress.

value.zh: 夏四月庚戌，處州賊犯崇安，殺都指揮吳剛。
value.en: In summer, the fourth month, on gengxu, Chuzhou bandits attacked Chong'an and killed Regional Commander Wu Gang.
value.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day gengxu, Chuzhou bandits attacked Chong'an and killed Regional Commander Wu Gang.

value.zh: 壬戌，湖廣、貴州苗賊大起，命王驥討之。
value.en: On renxu Miao bandits rose on a great scale in Huguang and Guizhou, and Wang Ji was ordered to attack them.
value.literal: On the day renxu, Miao bandits rose on a great scale in Huguang and Guizhou; Wang Ji was ordered to attack them.

value.zh: 乙丑，遣御史十三人同中官督福建、浙江銀課。
value.en: On yichou thirteen censors were sent with palace eunuchs to supervise the silver-mining levy in Fujian and Zhejiang.
value.literal: On the day yichou, thirteen censors were dispatched together with palace eunuchs to supervise the silver-mining levy in Fujian and Zhejiang.

value.zh: 五月丙戌，陳懋擊破沙縣賊。
value.en: In the fifth month, on bingxu, Chen Mao defeated the bandits of Shaxian.
value.literal: In the fifth month, on the day bingxu, Chen Mao defeated the bandits of Shaxian.

value.zh: 壬辰，旱，太監金英同法司錄囚。
value.en: On renchen drought struck; the eunuch Jin Ying joined the judiciary in reviewing prisoners.
value.literal: On the day renchen, there was drought; the eunuch Jin Ying together with the judiciary reviewed prisoners.

value.zh: 己亥，侍讀學士張益直文淵閣，預機務。
value.en: On jihai Zhang Yi, reader-in-waiting, was assigned direct duty at the Wenyuan Pavilion to share in deliberation.
value.literal: On the day jihai, Reader-in-waiting Zhang Yi was assigned direct duty at the Wenyuan Pavilion to deliberate on state affairs.

value.zh: 庚子，巡按福建御史汪澄棄市，并殺前巡按御史柴文顯。
value.en: On gengzi Fujian touring censor Wang Cheng was executed in the market, and the former touring censor Chai Wenxian was killed as well.
value.literal: On the day gengzi, Fujian touring censor Wang Cheng was executed in the market, and the former touring censor Chai Wenxian was also killed.

value.zh: 六月庚戌，靖州苗犯辰溪，都指揮高亮戰死。
value.en: In the sixth month, on gengxu, Jingzhou Miao attacked Chenxi and Regional Commander Gao Liang fell in battle.
value.literal: In the sixth month, on the day gengxu, Jingzhou Miao attacked Chenxi; Regional Commander Gao Liang died in battle.

value.zh: 丙辰，南京謹身諸殿災。
value.en: On bingchen several halls of the Jinshen complex in Nanjing burned.
value.literal: On the day bingchen, several halls of the Jinshen complex in Nanjing burned.

value.zh: 甲子，修省。
value.en: On jiazi the court undertook self-reform and austerity.
value.literal: On the day jiazi, the court undertook self-reform and austerity.

value.zh: 詔河南、山西班軍番休者盡赴大同、宣府．乙丑，西寧侯宋瑛總督大同兵馬。
value.en: An edict ordered Henan and Shanxi garrison troops on rotational leave to march to Datong and Xuanfu. On yichou Song Ying, Marquis of Xining, took command of military affairs at Datong.
value.literal: An edict ordered rotational-leave garrison troops of Henan and Shanxi all to proceed to Datong and Xuanfu. On the day yichou, Song Ying, Marquis of Xining, supervised military affairs at Datong.

value.zh: 己巳，赦天下。
value.en: On jisi a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
value.literal: On the day jisi, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

value.zh: 戊寅，平鄉伯陳懷，駙馬都尉井源，都督王貴、吳克勤，太監林壽，分練京軍於大同、宣府，備瓦剌。
value.en: On wuyin Chen Huai, Earl of Pingxiang, Chief Commandant-escort Jing Yuan, Commissioners Wang Gui and Wu Keqin, and the eunuch Lin Shou were assigned in separate parties to drill capital troops at Datong and Xuanfu against the Oirats.
value.literal: On the day wuyin, Chen Huai, Earl of Pingxiang, Chief Commandant-escort Jing Yuan, Commissioners Wang Gui and Wu Keqin, and the eunuch Lin Shou were assigned in separate parties to drill capital troops at Datong and Xuanfu in preparation against the Oirats.

value.zh: 秋七月己丑，瓦剌也先寇大同，參將吳浩戰死，下詔親征。
value.en: In the seventh month of autumn, on jichou, Esen of the Oirats raided Datong; Vice Commissioner Wu Hao fell in battle, and the throne ordered a personal campaign.
value.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jichou, Esen of the Oirats raided Datong; Vice Commissioner Wu Hao died in battle, and an edict ordered the Emperor's personal campaign.

value.zh: 吏部尚書王直帥羣臣諫，不聽。
value.en: Wang Zhi, minister of personnel, led the officials in remonstrance, but the emperor would not listen.
value.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi led the officials in remonstrance; this was not heeded.

value.zh: 癸巳，命郕王居守。
value.en: On guisi the Prince of Cheng was ordered to remain and guard the capital.
value.literal: On the day guisi, the Prince of Cheng was ordered to remain and guard the capital.

value.zh: 是日，西寧侯宋瑛、武進伯朱冕與瓦剌戰於陽和，敗沒。
value.en: That same day Song Ying, Marquis of Xining, and Zhu Mian, Earl of Wujin, fought the Oirats at Yanghe and were wiped out.
value.literal: That day Song Ying, Marquis of Xining, and Zhu Mian, Earl of Wujin, fought the Oirats at Yanghe and were defeated and lost.

value.zh: 甲午，發京師。
value.en: On jiawu the army set out from the capital.
value.literal: On the day jiawu, the army set out from the capital.

value.zh: 乙未，次龍虎臺，軍中夜驚。
value.en: On yiwei the host halted at Longhu Terrace, and the army panicked in the night.
value.literal: On the day yiwei, it halted at Longhu Terrace; there was a night alarm in the army.

value.zh: 丁酉，次居庸關。
value.en: On dingyou the host halted at Juyong Pass.
value.literal: On the day dingyou, it halted at Juyong Pass.

value.zh: 辛丑，次宣府。
value.en: On xinchou the host halted at Xuanfu.
value.literal: On the day xinchou, it halted at Xuanfu.

value.zh: 羣臣屢請駐蹕，不許。
value.en: The officials repeatedly begged him to halt his march, but he would not consent.
value.literal: The officials repeatedly asked that he halt his progress; this was not permitted.

value.zh: 丙午，次陽和。
value.en: On bingwu the host halted at Yanghe.
value.literal: On the day bingwu, it halted at Yanghe.

value.zh: 八月戊申，次大同。
value.en: In the eighth month, on wushen, the Emperor encamped at Datong.
value.literal: In the eighth month, on the day wushen, he halted at Datong.

value.zh: 鎮守太監郭敬諫，議旋師。
value.en: Defender-attendant eunuch Guo Jing remonstrated and urged a withdrawal.
value.literal: Guo Jing, the defender-attendant eunuch, remonstrated and urged withdrawal.

value.zh: 己酉，廣寧伯劉安為總兵官，鎮大同。
value.en: On jiyou Liu An, Baron of Guangning, was made overall commander and posted to Datong.
value.literal: On the day jiyou, Liu An, Baron of Guangning, was made commander-in-chief and stationed at Datong.

value.zh: 庚戌，師還。
value.en: On gengxu the army turned back.
value.literal: On the day gengxu, the army returned.

value.zh: 丁巳，次宣府。
value.en: On dingsi he encamped at Xuanfu.
value.literal: On the day dingsi, he halted at Xuanfu.

value.zh: 庚申，瓦剌兵大至，恭順侯吳克忠、都督吳克勤戰沒，成國公朱勇、永順伯薛綬救之，至鷂兒嶺遇伏，全軍盡覆。
value.en: On gengshen Oirat forces came in strength; Wu Kexiong, Marquis of Gongshun, and Regional Commander Wu Keqin fell in battle; Zhu Yong, Duke of Cheng, and Xue Sui, Earl of Yongshun, marched to relieve them but at Ya'er Ridge met an ambush and the entire host was wiped out.
value.literal: On the day gengshen, Oirat troops arrived in force; Marquis of Gongshun Wu Kexiong and Regional Commander Wu Keqin fell in battle; Duke of Cheng Zhu Yong and Earl of Yongshun Xue Sui went to their rescue—at Ya'er Ridge they met an ambush and the whole army was destroyed.

value.zh: 辛酉，次土木，被圍。
value.en: On xinyou he halted at Tumu and was surrounded.
value.literal: On the day xinyou, he halted at Tumu and was besieged.

value.zh: 壬戌，師潰，死者數十萬。
value.en: On renxu the army broke; deaths ran into the hundreds of thousands.
value.literal: On the day renxu, the army collapsed; several hundred thousand died.

value.zh: 英國公張輔，泰寧侯陳瀛，駙馬都尉井源，平鄉伯陳懷，襄城伯李珍，遂安伯陳塤，修武伯沈榮，都督梁成、王貴，尚書王佐、鄺埜，學士曹鼐、張益，侍郎丁鉉、王永和、[2]副都御史鄧棨等，皆死，帝北狩。
value.en: Zhang Fu, Duke of Ying; Chen Ying, Marquis of Taining; Jing Yuan, Commander of Horse; Chen Huai, Baron of Pingxiang; Li Zhen, Baron of Xiangcheng; Chen Kun, Baron of Suian; Shen Rong, Baron of Xiuwu; Regional Commanders Liang Cheng and Wang Gui; Ministers Wang Zuo and Kuang Ye; Academicians Cao Nai and Zhang Yi; Vice Ministers Ding Xuan and Wang Yonghe; and Vice Censor-in-chief Deng Qi, among others—all fell; the Emperor was borne north.
value.literal: Duke of Ying Zhang Fu, Marquis of Taining Chen Ying, Commander of Horse Jing Yuan, Baron of Pingxiang Chen Huai, Baron of Xiangcheng Li Zhen, Baron of Suian Chen Kun, Baron of Xiuwu Shen Rong, Regional Commanders Liang Cheng and Wang Gui, Ministers Wang Zuo and Kuang Ye, Academicians Cao Nai and Zhang Yi, Vice Ministers Ding Xuan and Wang Yonghe, [2] and Vice Censor-in-chief Deng Qi, among others—all perished; the Emperor went on a northern hunt.

value.zh: 甲子，京師聞敗，羣臣聚哭於朝，侍講徐珵請南遷，兵部侍郎于謙不可。
value.en: On jiazi word of defeat reached the capital; the court assembled in tears; Lecturer Xu Cheng urged removal to the south; Vice Minister Yu Qian forbade it.
value.literal: On the day jiazi, the capital heard of defeat; officials gathered weeping at court; Lecturer Xu Cheng proposed relocating south; Vice Minister of War Yu Qian forbade it.

value.zh: 乙丑，皇太后命郕王監國。
value.en: On yichou the Empress Dowager ordered the Prince of Cheng to oversee the realm as regent.
value.literal: On the day yichou, the Empress Dowager ordered the Prince of Cheng to act as regent.

value.zh: 戊辰，帝至大同。
value.en: On wuchen the captive Emperor reached Datong.
value.literal: On the day wuchen, the Emperor reached Datong.

value.zh: 己巳，皇太后命立皇子見深為皇太子。
value.en: On jisi the Empress Dowager had Zhu Jianshen named crown prince.
value.literal: On the day jisi, the Empress Dowager ordered the prince Jianshen established as Crown Prince.

value.zh: 辛未，帝至威寧海子。
value.en: On xinwei he came to Weining Lake.
value.literal: On the day xinwei, the Emperor reached Weining Lake.

value.zh: 甲戌，至黑河。
value.en: On jiaxu he reached the Black River.
value.literal: On the day jiaxu, he reached the Black River.

value.zh: 九月癸未，郕王即位，遙尊帝為太上皇帝。
value.en: In the ninth month, on guimao, the Prince of Cheng took the throne and from afar honored the captive as Retired Emperor.
value.literal: In the ninth month, on the day guimao, the Prince of Cheng ascended the throne and honored the Emperor from afar as Retired Emperor.

value.zh: 硃亮祖
value.en: Zhu Liangzu
value.literal: Zhu Liangzu

value.zh: 張翼，臨淮人。
value.en: Zhang Yi was a native of Linhuai.
value.literal: Zhang Yi was a man of Linhuai.

value.zh: 父聚，以前翼元帥從平江南、淮東，積功為大同衛指揮同知，致仕。
value.en: His father Ju had served as a wing marshal in the pacification of Jiangnan and Huaidong and, for accumulated merit, rose to vice commander of the Datong Guard before retiring.
value.literal: His father Ju, formerly a wing marshal, followed in the pacification of Jiangnan and Huaidong; through accumulated merit he became Vice Commander of the Datong Guard and retired.

value.zh: 翼隨父軍中，驍勇善戰，以副千戶嗣父職。
value.en: Yi followed his father in the army. Fierce and skilled in battle, he succeeded to his father's post as deputy centurion.
value.literal: Yi followed his father in the army, was fierce and skilled in battle, and as Deputy Centurion succeeded to his father's post.

value.zh: 從征陝西，擒叛寇。
value.en: He campaigned in Shaanxi and captured rebel bandits.
value.literal: He followed the campaign in Shaanxi and captured rebel bandits.

value.zh: 擢都指揮僉事，進僉都督府事。
value.en: He was promoted to associate regional commander and then to associate director of the chief military commission.
value.literal: He was promoted to Associate Regional Commander and advanced to Associate Director of the Chief Military Commission.

value.zh: 從藍玉征雲南，克普定、曲靖。
value.en: He followed Lan Yu into Yunnan and captured Puding and Qujing.
value.literal: He followed Lan Yu in the campaign against Yunnan and captured Puding and Qujing.

value.zh: 取鶴慶、麗江，剿七百房山寨。
value.en: He took Heqing and Lijiang and suppressed the stockades of the Seven Hundred Houses.
value.literal: He took Heqing and Lijiang and suppressed the stockades of the Seven Hundred Houses.

value.zh: 搗劍川，擊石門。
value.en: He raided Jianchuan and attacked Shimen.
value.literal: He raided Jianchuan and attacked Shimen.

value.zh: 十七年論功封鶴慶侯，祿二千五百石，予世券。
value.en: In the seventeenth year, for his merit, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Heqing with an income of 2,500 piculs of grain and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.
value.literal: In the seventeenth year, when merit was assessed, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Heqing with an income of two thousand five hundred piculs of grain and granted a hereditary patent.

value.zh: 二十六年坐玉黨死。
value.en: In the twenty-sixth year he was executed as a member of Yu's faction.
value.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was executed by association with Yu's faction.

value.zh: 曹鼐
value.en: Cao Nai
value.literal: Cao Nai

value.zh: 〈（張益鄺埜）〉
value.en: (Zhang Yi; Kuang Ye)〉
value.literal: (Zhang Yi; Kuang Ye)〉

value.zh: 王佐
value.en: Wang Zuo
value.literal: Wang Zuo

value.zh: 〈（丁鉉等）〉
value.en: (Ding Xian and others)〉
value.literal: (Ding Xian and others)〉

value.zh: 孫祥
value.en: Sun Xiang
value.literal: Sun Xiang

value.en: (Xie Ze)〉
value.literal: (Xie Ze)〉

value.zh: 袁彬
value.en: Yuan Bin
value.literal: Yuan Bin

value.zh: 〈（哈銘袁敏）〉
value.en: (Ha Ming; Yuan Min)〉
value.literal: (Ha Ming; Yuan Min)〉

value.zh: 十四年七月，也先入寇，中官王振挾帝親征。
value.en: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year, Esen of the Oirats invaded; the eunuch Wang Zhen pressed the Emperor to take the field in person.
value.literal: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year, Esen of the Oirats invaded; the eunuch Wang Zhen induced the Emperor to lead a campaign in person.

value.zh: 朝臣交章諫，不聽。
value.en: Officials of the court submitted memorial after memorial in protest, but he would not heed them.
value.literal: Court officials submitted memorial after memorial in remonstrance, but he would not listen.

value.zh: 鼐與張益以閣臣扈從。
value.en: Nai and Zhang Yi accompanied the campaign as Grand Secretariat ministers.
value.literal: Nai and Zhang Yi accompanied the expedition as Grand Secretariat ministers.

value.zh: 未至大同，士卒已乏糧。
value.en: Before they reached Datong, the soldiers were already without adequate grain.
value.literal: Before they reached Datong, the troops were already short of provisions.

value.zh: 宋瑛、朱冕全軍沒。
value.en: Song Ying and Zhu Mian were destroyed with their whole forces.
value.literal: Song Ying and Zhu Mian were wiped out with their entire armies.

value.zh: 諸臣請班師，振不許，趣諸軍進。
value.en: The ministers asked to withdraw the army; Zhen refused and pressed the troops to advance.
value.literal: The ministers asked to withdraw the army; Zhen would not permit it and urged the forces forward.

value.zh: 大將朱勇膝行聽命，尚書鄺埜、王佐跪草中，至暮不得請。
value.en: The commander Zhu Yong advanced on his knees to receive orders; the Ministers Kuang Ye and Wang Zuo knelt in the grass, yet until evening could not secure a hearing.
value.literal: The commander Zhu Yong crawled on his knees to receive orders; the Ministers Kuang Ye and Wang Zuo knelt in the grass, but until evening could not obtain an audience.

value.zh: 欽天監正彭德清言天象示警，若前，恐危乘輿。
value.en: The Director of the Astronomy Bureau Peng Deqing said the heavens showed warnings: if they proceeded as before, the imperial carriage might be imperiled.
value.literal: The Director of the Astronomy Bureau Peng Deqing said the heavens showed warnings: if they went on as before, the imperial carriage might be endangered.

value.zh: 振詈曰：「爾何知！
value.en: Zhen cursed him, saying: "What do you know!
value.literal: Zhen reviled him, saying: "What do you know!

value.zh: 若有此，亦天命也。」
value.en: If that should come to pass, it is likewise Heaven's mandate."
value.literal: If this should happen, it is also the mandate of Heaven."

value.zh: 鼐曰：「臣子固不足惜，主上系天下安危，豈可輕進？」
value.en: Nai said: "We subjects are not worth sparing, but Your Majesty holds the safety of the realm in your hands—how can you advance so lightly?"
value.literal: Nai said: "We subjects are indeed not worth sparing, but Your Majesty bears the safety of the realm—how can you lightly advance?"

value.zh: 振終不從。
value.en: Zhen in the end would not agree.
value.literal: Zhen in the end would not comply.

value.zh: 前驅敗報踵至，始懼，欲還。
value.en: Reports of defeat from the advance guard arrived in succession; he at last grew afraid and wished to turn back.
value.literal: Reports of defeat from the van arrived one after another; he at last grew afraid and wished to turn back.

value.zh: 定襄侯郭登言於鼐、益曰：「自此趨紫荊，裁四十餘里，駕宜從紫荊入。」
value.en: Guo Deng, Marquis of Dingxiang, said to Nai and Yi: "From here it is only a little over forty li to Zijing—the imperial carriage ought to enter by Zijing."
value.literal: Guo Deng, Marquis of Dingxiang, said to Nai and Yi: "From here it is only a little over forty li to Zijing—the carriage ought to enter by Zijing."

value.zh: 振欲邀帝至蔚州幸其第，不聽，復折而東，趨居庸。
value.en: Zhen wished to bring the Emperor to Yu Prefecture to visit his own house; the Emperor did not listen, and they turned east again toward Juyong.
value.literal: Zhen wished to invite the Emperor to Yu Prefecture to visit his own residence; the Emperor did not listen, and they turned east again toward Juyong.

value.zh: 八月辛酉次土木。
value.en: On the xinyou day of the eighth month they encamped at Tumu.
value.literal: On the xinyou day of the eighth month they halted at Tumu.

value.zh: 地高，掘地二丈不及水。
value.en: The ground was high; they dug two zhang deep but still did not reach water.
value.literal: The ground was high; they dug two zhang deep but still did not reach water.

value.zh: 瓦剌大至，據南河。
value.en: The Oirats arrived in strength and occupied the south bank of the river.
value.literal: The Oirats came in force and held the south bank of the river.

value.zh: 明日佯卻，且遣使通和。
value.en: The next day they feigned retreat and also sent envoys to discuss peace.
value.literal: The next day they feigned withdrawal and moreover sent envoys to negotiate peace.

value.zh: 帝召鼐草詔答之。
value.en: The Emperor summoned Nai to draft an edict in response.
value.literal: The Emperor summoned Nai to draft an edict in reply.

value.zh: 振遽令移營就水，行亂。
value.en: Zhen abruptly ordered the camp shifted toward the water, and the army fell into disorder.
value.literal: Zhen abruptly ordered the camp moved toward the water, and the march fell into disorder.

value.zh: 寇騎蹂陣入，帝突圍不得出，擁以去。
value.en: Enemy horsemen overran the formation; the Emperor could not break out and was seized and borne away.
value.literal: Enemy horsemen trampled through the formation; the Emperor could not break out and was seized and carried away.

value.zh: 鼐、益等俱及於難。
value.en: Nai, Yi, and the others all perished in the disaster.
value.literal: Nai, Yi, and the others all met disaster.

value.zh: 景帝立，贈鼐少傅、吏部尚書、文淵閣大學士，謚文襄，官其子恩大理評事。
value.en: When the Jing Emperor took the throne, Nai was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, with the posthumous title Wenxiang; his son En was appointed Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.
value.literal: When the Jing Emperor ascended the throne, Nai was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, with the posthumous title Wenxiang; his son En was given office as Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.

value.zh: 英宗復位，加贈太傅，改謚文忠，復官其孫榮錦衣百戶。
value.en: When Emperor Ying regained the throne, Nai was further posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and his posthumous title changed to Wenzhong; his grandson Rong was again appointed a commander of one hundred households in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
value.literal: When Emperor Ying restored the throne, he was further posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and his posthumous title changed to Wenzhong; his grandson Rong was again given office as commander of one hundred households in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

value.zh: 鼐弟鼎進士，歷吏科都給事中。
value.en: Nai's younger brother Ding was a metropolitan graduate and rose to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.
value.literal: Nai's younger brother Ding was a metropolitan graduate and served successively as Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.

value.zh: 張益，字士謙，江寧人。
value.en: Zhang Yi, styled Shiqian, came from Jiangning.
value.literal: Zhang Yi, styled Shiqian, was a native of Jiangning.

value.zh: 永樂十三年進士。
value.en: In the thirteenth year of Yongle he passed the metropolitan examination.
value.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongle he became a metropolitan graduate.

value.zh: 由庶吉士授中書舍人，改大理評事。
value.en: From Hanlin Bachelor he was appointed Secretariat Drafter, then moved to Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.
value.literal: From Student of the Hanlin he was appointed Secretariat Drafter, then transferred to be Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.

value.zh: 與修《宣宗實錄》成，改修撰。
value.en: When the Veritable Records of the Xuande Emperor were finished, he was made Compiler.
value.literal: When the Veritable Records of the Xuande Emperor were completed, he was made Compiler.

value.zh: 博學強記，詩文操筆立就，三楊雅重之。
value.en: He was learned and had a powerful memory; his verse and prose were finished the moment he set brush to paper, and the Three Yangs greatly valued him.
value.literal: He was broadly learned and had a strong memory; his poetry and prose were completed as soon as he took up the brush, and the Three Yangs held him in high esteem.

value.zh: 尋進侍讀學士，正統十四年入文淵閣。
value.en: He was soon promoted to Reader-in-Waiting and in the fourteenth year of Zhengtong entered the Wenyuan Pavilion.
value.literal: Soon he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting and in the fourteenth year of Zhengtong entered the Wenyuan Pavilion.

value.zh: 未三月，遽蒙難以歿。
value.en: In less than three months he suddenly met disaster and died.
value.literal: In less than three months he suddenly met disaster and died.

value.zh: 景帝立，贈學士，謚文僖。
value.en: When the Jing Emperor took the throne, he was posthumously granted the title of Academician, with the posthumous name Wenxi.
value.literal: When the Jing Emperor ascended the throne, he was posthumously given the title of Academician, with the posthumous name Wenxi.

value.zh: 曾孫琮進士。
value.en: His great-grandson Cong passed the metropolitan examination.
value.literal: His great-grandson Cong was a metropolitan graduate.

value.zh: 嘉靖初歷官南京右都御史。
value.en: Early in the Jiajing reign he rose to Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he served successively as Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.

value.zh: 費宏
value.en: Fei Hong
value.literal: Fei Hong

value.zh: 〈（弟寀從子懋中子懋賢世父瑄）〉
value.en: (His younger brother Cai, his nephew Maozhong, his son Maoxian, and his clan elder father Xuan)〉
value.literal: (Younger brother Cai; nephew Maozhong; son Maoxian; clan elder father Xuan)〉

value.zh: 翟鑾李時顧鼎臣嚴訥
value.en: Zhai Luan, Li Shi, Gu Dingchen, and Yan Ne
value.literal: Zhai Luan, Li Shi, Gu Dingchen, Yan Ne

value.en: (Yuan Wei)〉
value.literal: (Yuan Wei)〉

value.zh: 李春芳
value.en: Li Chunfang
value.literal: Li Chunfang

value.zh: 〈（孫思誠等）〉
value.en: (Sun Sicheng and others)〉
value.literal: (Sun Sicheng and others)〉

value.zh: 陳以勤趙貞吉
value.en: Chen Yiqin and Zhao Zhenji
value.literal: Chen Yiqin, Zhao Zhenji

value.zh: 〈（殷士儋）〉
value.en: (Yin Shidan)〉
value.literal: (Yin Shidan)〉

value.zh: 高儀
value.en: Gao Yi
value.literal: Gao Yi

value.zh: 四十年，遷至戶部右侍郎。
value.en: In the fortieth year he rose to vice minister of revenue on the right.
value.literal: In the fortieth year he rose to vice minister of revenue on the right.

value.zh: 廷議遣大臣赴薊州督餉練兵，嵩欲用貞吉，召飲示之意。
value.en: The court debated sending a high minister to Jizhou to supervise grain transport and drill troops; Song wished to use Zhenji and summoned him to drink and show his intent.
value.literal: The court debated sending a high minister to Jizhou to supervise grain transport and drill troops; Song wished to use Zhenji and summoned him to drink and show his intent.

value.zh: 貞吉曰：「督餉者，督京運乎，民運乎？
value.en: Zhenji said, "Does supervising grain mean capital transport or civilian transport?
value.literal: Zhenji said: "Does supervising grain mean supervising capital transport, or civilian transport?

value.zh: 若二運已有職掌，添官徒增擾耳。
value.en: If both already have responsible offices, adding officials only increases disturbance.
value.literal: If both already have responsible offices, adding officials only increases disturbance.

value.zh: 況兵之不練，其過宜不在是，即十戶侍出，何益練兵？」
value.en: Moreover, if troops are not drilled, the fault should not lie here. Even ten household stewards sent out would not help drill troops."
value.literal: Moreover, if troops are not drilled, the fault should not lie here. Even ten household stewards sent out would not help drill troops."

value.zh: 嵩怫然罷。
value.en: Song left displeased.
value.literal: Song left displeased.

value.zh: 會嵩請告，吏部用倉場侍郎林應亮。
value.en: When Song requested leave the Ministry of Personnel appointed the granary vice minister Lin Yingliang.
value.literal: When Song requested leave the Ministry of Personnel appointed the granary vice minister Lin Yingliang.

value.zh: 比嵩出，益怒。
value.en: When Song came out he was still more angry.
value.literal: When Song came out he was still more angry.

value.zh: 令都給事中張益劾應亮，調之南京，而改用僉都御史霍冀。
value.en: He had the supervising secretary Zhang Yi impeach Yingliang and transfer him to Nanjing, and instead used the vice censor-in-chief Huo Ji.
value.literal: He had the supervising secretary Zhang Yi impeach Yingliang and transfer him to Nanjing, and instead used the vice censor-in-chief Huo Ji.

value.zh: 益又言：「督餉戶部專職，今貞吉與左侍郎劉大賓廷推不及，是不職也，宜罷。」
value.en: Yi also said: "Supervising grain is the special duty of the Ministry of Revenue. Now Zhenji and left vice minister Liu Dabin were not reached in court recommendation; this is dereliction and they ought to be dismissed."
value.literal: Yi also said: "Supervising grain is the special duty of the Ministry of Revenue. Now Zhenji and left vice minister Liu Dabin were not reached in court recommendation; this is dereliction and they ought to be dismissed."

value.zh: 於是二人皆奪官。
value.en: Thereupon both men were stripped of office.
value.literal: Thereupon both men were stripped of office.

value.zh: 韃靼，即蒙古，故元後也。
value.en: The Tartars are the Mongols—the remnant house of the Yuan.
value.literal: The Tartars are the Mongols, the successors of the former Yuan.

value.zh: 太祖洪武元年，大將軍徐達率師取元，元主自北平遁出塞，居開平，數遣其將也速等擾北邊。
value.en: In the founding emperor’s first Hongwu year, Grand General Xu Da marched to seize the Yuan capital; the Yuan emperor slipped from Beiping north of the passes and made Kaiping his seat, while repeatedly dispatching generals such as Yisu to raid the northern border.
value.literal: In the first year of Hongwu under the founding emperor, Grand General Xu Da led troops to take the Yuan; the Yuan ruler fled from Beiping out beyond the passes, dwelt at Kaiping, and repeatedly sent his generals Yisu and others to harass the northern frontier.

value.zh: 明年，常遇春擊敗之，師進開平，俘宗王慶孫、平章鼎住。
value.en: The following year Chang Yuchun routed them; the army pushed on to Kaiping and took the imperial prince Qing Sun and Chancellor Dingzhu prisoner.
value.literal: The next year Chang Yuchun defeated them; the army advanced to Kaiping and captured the imperial prince Qing Sun and the chancellor Dingzhu.

value.zh: 明年，北部亦卜剌與小王子仇殺。
value.en: The following year Yibulai of the north and the Little Prince turned on each other.
value.literal: The next year Yibulai of the northern tribes and the Little Prince feuded and fought each other.

value.zh: 亦卜剌竄西海，阿爾禿廝與合，逼脅洮西屬番，屢入寇。
value.en: Yibulai fled to the Western Sea, allied with Aertusi, bullied the dependent tribes west of the Tao, and raided again and again.
value.literal: Yibulai fled to the Western Sea, joined with Aertusi, coerced the dependent tribes west of the Tao River, and repeatedly entered in raids.

value.zh: 巡撫張翼、總兵王勳不能制，漸深入，邊人苦之。
value.en: Grand Coordinator Zhang Yi and Commander Wang Xun could not check them; the raids pushed ever deeper, and the border people suffered.
value.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhang Yi and Commander-in-Chief Wang Xun could not control them; they gradually penetrated deeper, and frontier people suffered bitterly.

value.zh: 八年夏，擁眾來川，遣使詣翼所，乞邊地駐牧修貢。
value.en: In the eighth year, that summer, he brought a large force into the frontier valleys and sent envoys to Zhang Yi asking for pasturelands and permission to resume tribute.
value.literal: In the summer of the eighth year he gathered a host and came to the frontier riverlands, sent envoys to Yi's headquarters, and begged for border land to pasture and restore tribute.

value.zh: 翼啖以金帛，令遠徙，亦卜剌遂西掠烏斯藏，據之。
value.en: Zhang Yi placated him with gold and silk and told him to move on; Yibulai then swept west into Tibet and seized the region.
value.literal: Yi enticed him with gold and silks and ordered him to move far away; Yibulai then raided west into U-Tsang and occupied it.

value.zh: 自是洮、岷、松潘無寧歲。
value.en: After that Tao, Min, and Songpan knew no quiet year.
value.literal: From this time Tao, Min, and Songpan had no peaceful year.

value.zh: 蔣琬字公琰，零陵湘鄉人也。
value.en: Jiang Wan, courtesy name Gongyan, came from Xiangxiang in Lingling Commandery.
value.literal: Jiang Wan, courtesy name Gongyan, was a native of Xiangxiang in Lingling.

value.zh: 弱冠與外弟泉陵劉敏懼知名。
value.en: While still young he won local fame alongside his cousin Liu Min of Quanling.
value.literal: While still young he won local fame alongside his cousin Liu Min of Quanling.

value.zh: 琬以州書佐隨先主入蜀，除廣都長。
value.en: He entered Shu as a provincial clerk under Liu Bei and was named magistrate of Guangdu.
value.literal: Wan served as a provincial clerk and followed the Vanguard Lord into Shu; he was appointed magistrate of Guangdu.

value.zh: 先主嘗因遊觀奄至廣都，見琬眾事不理，時又沉醉，先主大怒，將加罪戮。
value.en: Liu Bei came to Guangdu on a tour, found Jiang Wan drunk and neglecting his duties, and was ready to execute him.
value.literal: The Vanguard Lord once on a pleasure outing suddenly arrived at Guangdu and saw Wan leaving official business unattended and at the time also deeply drunk; the Vanguard Lord was greatly angry and was about to impose punishment and execution.

value.zh: 軍師將軍諸葛亮請曰：「蔣琬，社稷之器，非百里之才也。
value.en: Zhuge Liang intervened: "Jiang Wan is material for the empire, not a petty county magistrate.
value.literal: Army commander Zhuge Liang pleaded, saying, "Jiang Wan is vessel of the altars of soil and grain—not talent for a hundred li.

value.zh: 其為政以安民為本，不以修飾為先，願主公重加察之。」
value.en: He rules by putting the people at ease, not by polished appearances—please look again, my lord."
value.literal: His governing takes pacifying the people as root, not ornament as first; wish the lord examine him again carefully."

value.zh: 先主雅敬亮，乃不加罪，倉卒但免官而已。
value.en: Liu Bei yielded to Zhuge Liang and spared him—stripping him of office alone.
value.literal: The Vanguard Lord always respected Liang and therefore did not add punishment; in haste he only dismissed from office.

value.zh: 琬見推之後，夜夢有—牛頭在門前，流血滂沱，意甚惡之，呼問占夢趙直。
value.en: After his promotion Jiang Wan dreamed of a bloody ox head at his gate and consulted Zhao Zhi about it.
value.literal: After Wan was promoted, he dreamed at night of an ox head before the gate, bleeding profusely—his intent felt very ill; he called to ask dream-diviner Zhao Zhi.

value.zh: 直曰：「夫見血者，事分明也。
value.en: Zhi said, "Seeing blood means affairs are clear-cut.
value.literal: Zhi said, "Seeing blood means affairs are clear-cut.

value.zh: 牛角及鼻，『公』字之象，君位必當至公，大吉之征也。」
value.en: Horns and snout sketch the word ‘duke’—you are destined for high, impartial office; most auspicious."
value.literal: Ox horn and nose are images of the character ‘public’; your position must reach utmost fairness—a greatly auspicious sign."

value.zh: 頃之，為什邡令。
value.en: Soon he was appointed magistrate of Shifang.
value.literal: Shortly thereafter he became magistrate of Shifang.

value.zh: 先主為漢中王，琬人為尚書郎。
value.en: When Liu Bei took the title King of Hanzhong, Jiang Wan became a secretary in the imperial secretariat.
value.literal: When the Vanguard Lord became King of Hanzhong, Wan entered as gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

value.zh: 建興元年，丞相亮開府，辟琬為東曹掾。
value.en: In Jianxing 1 (223 CE) Chancellor Zhuge Liang opened his headquarters and appointed Jiang Wan clerk of the eastern bureau.
value.literal: Jianxing first year, Chancellor Liang opened office, summoned Wan as eastern bureau clerk.

value.zh: 舉茂才，琬固讓劉邕、陰化、龐延、廖淳，亮教答曰：「思惟背親捨德，以殄百姓，眾人既不隱於心，實又使遠近不解其義，是以君宜顯其功舉，以明此選之清重也。」
value.en: Nominated as "abundant talent," Jiang Wan insisted the honor go to Liu Yong, Yin Hua, Pang Yan, or Liao Chun. Zhuge Liang answered: "If worthy men hid their light and turned their backs on the people, neither the court nor the countryside would understand—accept the nomination and show how seriously this selection is taken."
value.literal: Recommended abundant talent—Wan firmly yielded to Liu Yong, Yin Hua, Pang Yan, Liao Chun; Liang instructed reply saying: "Thinking consider betray kin abandon virtue, thereby destroy hundred surnames—crowd already not hidden in heart; truly also cause far near not understand its meaning—therefore lord should display this merit recommendation, thereby clarify this selection's purity weight."

value.zh: 遷為參軍。
value.en: He was promoted to army adviser.
value.literal: Then transferred as army adviser.

value.zh: 五年，亮住漢中，琬與長史張裔統留府事。
value.en: In the fifth year (227 CE) Zhuge Liang moved to Hanzhong; Jiang Wan and chief clerk Zhang Yi ran the rear headquarters.
value.literal: Fifth year, Liang dwelt Hanzhong; Wan together with chief clerk Zhang Yi governed remaining office affairs.

value.zh: 八年，代裔為長史，加撫軍將軍。
value.en: In the eighth year he succeeded Zhang Yi as chief clerk and received the title general who stabilizes the army.
value.literal: Eighth year, replaced Yi as chief clerk; added general who stabilizes the army.

value.zh: 亮數外出，琬常足食足兵以相供給。
value.en: Whenever Zhuge Liang marched out, Jiang Wan kept grain and weapons flowing without fail.
value.literal: Liang repeatedly went out abroad; Wan constantly full food full weapons thereby mutually supplied.

value.zh: 亮每言：「公琰托志忠雅，當與吾共贊王業者也。」
value.en: Zhuge Liang often said, "Gongyan is loyal and cultivated—he is the man to help me sustain the kingly enterprise."
value.literal: Liang each time said: "Gongyan entrusts ambition loyal refined—ought with me together assist kingly enterprise."

value.zh: 密表後主曰：「臣若不幸，後事宜以付琬。」
value.en: He secretly memorialized the emperor: "If I die, let Jiang Wan carry what follows."
value.literal: Secret memorial Later Lord saying: "Your servant if unlucky—after affairs should entrust to Wan."

value.zh: 五年，維率眾出漢。
value.en: In the fifth year of the Jingyao era (262) he led the army out from Hanzhong.
value.literal: Fifth year—Wei led the host out from Han.

value.zh: 侯和為鄧艾所破，還住沓中。
value.en: Deng Ai scattered him at Hehe; Jiang Wei fell back to Tazhong.
value.literal: He was defeated at Hehe by Deng Ai and withdrew to garrison Tazhong.

value.zh: 維本羈旅托國，累年攻戰，功績不立。
value.en: A northerner serving Shu, he campaigned endlessly with little to show for it.
value.literal: Wei was by nature a wanderer relying on the state—year after year attacking yet merit not established.

value.zh: 而宦官黃皓等弄權於內，右大將軍閻宇與皓協比，而皓陰欲廢維樹宇。
value.en: Court eunuch Huang Hao meddled at court; Yan Yu curried favor with him while Huang schemed to replace Jiang Wei.
value.literal: Yet eunuch Huang Hao and others wielded power within; General of the Right Yan Yu colluded with Hao—and Hao secretly wished to dismiss Wei and raise Yu.

value.zh: 維亦疑之，故自危懼，不復還成都。
value.en: Jiang Wei feared court intrigue and stayed away from Chengdu.
value.literal: Wei also suspected this—therefore lived in peril fear—no longer returned to Chengdu.

value.zh: 〈《华阳国志》曰；
value.en: < The Huayang Guo Zhi relates:
value.literal: < The Huayang Guo Zhi records:

value.zh: 维恶黄皓恣擅，启后主欲杀之。
value.en: Jiang Wei denounced Huang Hao’s excess and asked Liu Shan to execute him.
value.literal: Wei detested Huang Hao's wantonness and memorialized the Later Lord wishing to kill him.

value.zh: 后主曰：“皓趋走小臣耳，往董允切齿，吾常恨之，君何足介意！”
value.en: Liu Shan dismissed him: "Huang Hao is a mere runner—Dong Yun hated him too, yet I kept him—why fuss?"
value.literal: The Later Lord said, "Hao is only a running petty minister—long ago Dong Yun gnashed teeth at him—I always resented that—why should you care!"

value.zh: 维见皓枝附叶连，惧於失言，逊辞而出。
value.en: Seeing Huang Hao’s network, Jiang Wei held his tongue and withdrew politely.
value.literal: Wei saw Hao's branches attached leaves connected—feared misspeaking—yielding words and departed.

value.zh: 后主敕皓诣维陈谢。
value.en: Liu Shan sent Huang Hao to apologize to Jiang Wei.
value.literal: The Later Lord ordered Hao to go to Wei and declare apology.

value.zh: 维说皓求沓中种麦，以避内逼耳。〉
value.en: Jiang Wei asked leave to grow grain at Tazhong and escape court cabals.>
value.literal: Wei persuaded Hao to seek wheat planting at Tazhong—to avoid inner pressure.>

value.zh: 六年，維表後主：「聞鐘會治兵關中，欲規進取，宜並遣張翼、廖化詣督堵軍分護陽安關口、陰平橋頭，以防未然。」
value.en: In the sixth year, Jiang Wei memorialized the Later Lord: "I hear that Zhong Hui is training troops in Guanzhong and intends to make an advance. Zhang Yi and Liao Hua should be sent at once to command blocking forces, separately guarding the Yang'an pass and the bridgehead at Yinping, so as to forestall what has not yet happened."
value.literal: Sixth year—Wei memorialized the Later Lord: "I hear Zhong Hui trains troops in Guanzhong—intends to strike—we ought together dispatch Zhang Yi and Liao Hua to various supervisors to divide guard Yang'an pass and Yinping bridge—to guard before it happens."

value.zh: 皓徵信鬼巫，謂敌終不自致。
value.en: Huang Hao trusted sorcerers who swore the enemy would never march.
value.literal: Hao trusted ghost shamans—said the enemy in the end would not come of themselves.

value.zh: 啟後主寢其事，而群臣不知。
value.en: Liu Shan buried the memorial; the court never heard of it.
value.literal: He had the Later Lord sleep on the matter—and the host of ministers knew not.

value.zh: 及鐘會將向駱谷，鄧艾將入沓中。
value.en: When Zhong Hui entered Lu Valley and Deng Ai struck Tazhong,
value.literal: By the time Zhong Hui was bound for Lu Valley and Deng Ai for Tazhong—

value.zh: 然後乃遣右車騎廖化詣沓中為維援，左車騎張翼、輔國大將軍董厥等詣陽安關口以為諸圍外助。
value.en: relief came late: Liao Hua toward Tazhong, Zhang Yi and Dong Jue toward Yang’an.
value.literal: only then sent General of the Right Cavalry Liao Hua to Tazhong as aid to Wei—General of the Left Cavalry Zhang Yi and Defender-in-Chief Dong Jue and others to Yang'an pass as outer help for the ramparts.

value.zh: 比至陰平，聞魏將諸葛緒向建威，故住待之。
value.en: At Yinping he learned Zhuge Xu was aiming at Jianwei and paused.
value.literal: Reaching Yinping—heard Wei general Zhuge Xu was heading for Jianwei—therefore halted to await.

value.zh: 月餘，維為鄧艾所摧，還住陰平。
value.en: A month later Deng Ai broke him and he fell back to Yinping.
value.literal: After more than a month—Wei was crushed by Deng Ai—withdrew to Yinping.

value.zh: 鐘會攻圍漢、樂二城，遣別將進攻關口，蔣舒開城出降，傅僉格鬥而死。
value.en: Zhong Hui stormed Hanxing and Lecheng and sent a column at the pass—Jiang Shu surrendered while Fu Qian died fighting.
value.literal: Zhong Hui attacked and besieged Han and Le two cities—sent a separate general to advance on the pass—Jiang Shu opened the city to surrender—Fu Qian wrestled and died.

value.zh: 〈汉晋春秋曰：蒋舒将出降，乃诡谓傅佥曰：“今贼至不击而闭城自守，非良图也。”
value.en: < The Han–Jin Annals: Jiang Shu meant to defect and lied to Fu Qian: "Holding the gates without fighting helps no one."
value.literal: < The Han–Jin Annals says: Jiang Shu was about to surrender—deceitfully said to Fu Qian, "Now the bandits arrive—not striking yet closing the city to self-defend—is not a good plan."

value.zh: 佥曰：“受命保城，惟全为功，今违命出战，若丧师负国，死无益矣。”
value.en: Fu Qian answered: "Our orders are to hold—sortie risks defeat and dishonors the realm."
value.literal: Qian said, "Ordered to guard the city—only completeness is merit—now disobeying order to go out—if we lose the army and betray the state—death is without benefit."

value.zh: 舒曰：“子以保城获全为功，我以出战克敌为功，请各行其志。”
value.en: Jiang Shu said: "You call defense victory—I call a sortie victory—do as you believe."
value.literal: Shu said, "You take guarding the city and achieving completeness as merit—I take going out and defeating the enemy as merit—pray each walk his will."

value.zh: 遂率众出。
value.en: Then he marched out with his men.
value.literal: Thereupon led the host out.

value.zh: 佥谓其战也，至阴平，以降胡烈。
value.en: Fu Qian thought it a real attack; Jiang Shu slipped to Yinping and surrendered to Hu Lie.
value.literal: Qian thought he went to battle—reaching Yinping—surrendered to Hu Lie.

value.zh: 烈乘虚袭城，佥格斗而死，魏人义之。
value.en: Hu Lie seized the open gate; Fu Qian fought to the death and earned Wei’s respect.
value.literal: Lie rode emptiness to raid the city—Qian wrestled and died—Wei men deemed him righteous.

value.zh: 蜀记曰：蒋舒为武兴督，在事无称。
value.en: The Shu Ji adds that Jiang Shu had performed poorly as Wuxing commander.
value.literal: Shu Ji says: Jiang Shu was overseer of Wuxing—without distinction in office.

value.zh: 蜀命人代之，因留舒助汉中守。
value.en: Shu replaced him but kept him to help defend Hanzhong.
value.literal: Shu ordered a man to replace him—thereupon retained Shu to assist Hanzhong defense.

value.zh: 舒恨，故开城出降。〉
value.en: Bitter at the snub, Jiang Shu opened the gates to the enemy.>
value.literal: Shu resented—therefore opened the city to surrender.>

value.zh: 會攻樂城，不能克。
value.en: Zhong Hui failed to storm Lecheng.
value.literal: Hui attacked Le city—could not overcome.

value.zh: 聞關口已下，長驅而前，翼、厥甫至漢壽，維、化亦捨陰平而退。
value.en: When the pass fell Zhong Hui drove deep; Zhang Yi and Dong Jue had only reached Hanshou while Jiang Wei and Liao Hua quit Yinping.
value.literal: Hearing the pass had fallen—long drove forward—Yi, Jue had just reached Hanshou—Wei, Hua also abandoned Yinping and withdrew.

value.zh: 適與翼、厥合，皆退保劍閣以拒會。
value.en: They united at Jiange and blocked Zhong Hui.
value.literal: Happening to join Yi, Jue—all retreated to guard Jiange to resist Hui.

value.zh: 會與維書曰：「公侯以文武之德，懷邁世之略，功濟巴、漢、聲暢華夏，遠近莫不歸名。
value.en: Zhong Hui wrote to Jiang Wei, saying, "You possess both civil and martial virtue and hold strategies that rise above the age. Your achievements have aided Ba and Han, and your reputation resounds through China; near and far, all acknowledge your name.
value.literal: Hui wrote Wei a letter, saying, "Lordship with civil and martial virtue—embracing transcendent age strategy—merit bridges Ba and Han—fame rings Huaxia—far and near none do not submit name.

value.zh: 每惟疇昔，嘗同大化，吳札、鄭喬，能喻斯好。」
value.en: Each thinks on past days—once shared great transformation—Wu Zha, Zheng Qiao—can illustrate this friendship."
value.literal: Each thinks on past days—once shared great transformation—Wu Zha, Zheng Qiao—can illustrate this friendship."

value.zh: 維不答書，列營守險。
value.en: Jiang Wei ignored the letter and manned the narrows.
value.literal: Wei did not answer the letter—arrayed camps guarding the defile.

value.zh: 會不能克，糧運縣遠，將議還歸。
value.en: Zhong Hui stalled; supplies stretched thin and withdrawal loomed.
value.literal: Hui could not overcome—grain transport hung far—generals debated returning.

value.zh: 而鄧艾自陰平由景谷道傍入，遂破諸葛瞻於綿竹。
value.en: Deng Ai cut through Yinping’s side valley and crushed Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu.
value.literal: Yet Deng Ai from Yinping by Jinggu side path slipped in—thereupon broke Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu.

value.zh: 後主請降於艾，艾前據成都。
value.en: Liu Shan surrendered to Deng Ai, who marched into Chengdu.
value.literal: The Later Lord requested surrender to Ai—Ai advanced and occupied Chengdu.

value.zh: 維等初聞瞻破，或聞後主欲固守成都，或聞欲東入吳，或聞欲南人建寧。
value.en: Rumors flew: Liu Shan might hold Chengdu, flee to Wu, or bolt south to Jianning.
value.literal: Wei and others first heard Zhan broken—or heard the Later Lord wished to firm defend Chengdu—or heard wished to east enter Wu—or heard wished to south enter Jianning.

value.zh: 於是引軍由廣漢、郪道以審虛實。
value.en: Jiang Wei marched through Guanghan toward Qi to learn the truth.
value.literal: Thereupon led army by Guanghan, Qishan road—to examine emptiness and substance.

value.zh: 尋被後主敕令乃投戈放甲，詣會於涪軍前，將士鹹怒，拔刀斫石。
value.en: Liu Shan’s order to disarm reached him at Fu; his troops wept and struck rocks with their swords.
value.literal: Soon received Later Lord order—then cast aside weapons, loosened armor—went to Hui before Fu army—generals all angry—drew blades and hacked stone.

value.zh: 干寶《晋纪》云：会谓维曰；
value.en: < Gan Bao’s Jin Annals: Zhong Hui asked Jiang Wei—
value.literal: < Gan Bao's Jin Ji records: Hui said to Wei—

value.zh: “来何迟也？”
value.en: "Why so late?"
value.literal: "Why did you come so late?"

value.zh: 维正色流涕曰：“今日见此为速矣！”
value.en: Jiang Wei answered through tears: "To meet this moment is soon enough!"
value.literal: Wei with stern color weeping said, "Today to see this—is already swift!"

value.zh: 会甚奇之。〉
value.en: Zhong Hui marveled at him.>
value.literal: Hui greatly marveled.>

value.zh: 張儀者，魏人也。
value.en: Zhang Yi was a native of Wei.
value.literal: Zhang Yi was a man of Wei.

value.zh: 始嘗與蘇秦俱事鬼谷先生，學術，蘇秦自以不及張儀。
value.en: In his youth, he studied the arts of persuasion alongside Su Qin under Master Guigu of Ghost Valley. Su Qin always considered himself inferior to Zhang Yi.
value.literal: In his youth, he studied the arts of persuasion alongside Su Qin under Master Guigu. Su Qin always considered himself inferior to Zhang Yi.

value.zh: 張儀已學游說諸侯。
value.en: After Zhang Yi had completed his studies, he traveled among the feudal lords as a persuader.
value.literal: Once Zhang Yi had mastered the arts of diplomatic persuasion, he traveled among the feudal lords.

value.zh: 嘗從楚相飲，已而楚相亡璧，門下意張儀，曰：「儀貧無行，必此盜相君之璧。」
value.en: Once he drank with the prime minister of Chu. Later, the prime minister discovered that his precious jade disc was missing. His attendants suspected Zhang Yi, saying, "Zhang Yi is poor and of questionable character—he must have stolen the prime minister's jade disc."
value.literal: He once drank with the Prime Minister of Chu. Later, the prime minister discovered his precious jade disc was missing. His attendants suspected Zhang Yi, saying, 'Zhang Yi is poor and of questionable character—he must have stolen the prime minister's jade disc.'

value.zh: 共執張儀，掠笞數百，不服，醳之。
value.en: They seized Zhang Yi and flogged him several hundred times. When he still refused to confess, they released him.
value.literal: They seized Zhang Yi and flogged him several hundred times, but he refused to confess, so they branded him instead.

value.zh: 其妻曰：「嘻！
value.en: His wife said, "Alas!
value.literal: His wife said, 'Alas!

value.zh: 子毋讀書游說，安得此辱乎？」
value.en: If you had not studied books and traveled as a persuader, how would you have come to this humiliation?"
value.literal: If you hadn't studied and traveled as a persuader, how would you have come to this humiliation?'

value.zh: 張儀謂其妻曰：「視吾舌尚在不？」
value.en: Zhang Yi asked his wife, "Is my tongue still there?"
value.literal: Zhang Yi asked his wife, 'Is my tongue still there?'

value.zh: 其妻笑曰：「舌在也。」
value.en: His wife laughed and said, "It's still there."
value.literal: His wife laughed and said, 'It's still there.'

value.zh: 儀曰：「足矣。」
value.en: Zhang Yi replied, "That's enough."
value.literal: Zhang Yi replied, 'That's enough.'

value.zh: 蘇秦已說趙王而得相約從親，然恐秦之攻諸侯，敗約後負，念莫可使用於秦者，乃使人微感張儀曰：「子始與蘇秦善，今秦已當路，子何不往游，以求通子之願？」
value.en: After Su Qin had persuaded the King of Zhao and secured alliances with neighboring states for united action, he worried that Qin might attack the other lords and break the alliances. Thinking of who might be useful in Qin, he secretly sent someone to sound out Zhang Yi: "You were once close to Su Qin. Now Qin holds power—why not go there to seek your fortune?"
value.literal: After Su Qin had persuaded the King of Zhao and secured alliances with neighboring states, he worried that Qin might attack the other lords and break the alliances. Thinking of who might be useful in Qin, he secretly sent someone to tempt Zhang Yi: 'You were once close to Su Qin. Now Qin holds power—why not go there to seek your fortune?'

value.zh: 張儀於是之趙，上謁求見蘇秦。
value.en: Zhang Yi accordingly went to Zhao and requested an audience with Su Qin.
value.literal: Zhang Yi then traveled to Zhao and sought an audience with Su Qin.

value.zh: 蘇秦乃誡門下人不為通，又使不得去者數日。
value.en: Su Qin instructed his attendants not to announce Zhang Yi, and made him wait for several days without allowing him to leave.
value.literal: Su Qin ordered his attendants not to announce him, and kept him waiting for several days without letting him leave.

value.zh: 已而見之，坐之堂下，賜仆妾之食。
value.en: At last, when Su Qin received him, he seated Zhang Yi below the hall and gave him the fare of servants and concubines.
value.literal: Finally, when he received him, he seated Zhang Yi below the main platform and served him food meant for servants and concubines.

value.zh: 因而數讓之曰：「以子之材能，乃自令困辱至此。
value.en: Then he repeatedly rebuked him, saying, "With your talents and abilities, you have brought yourself to this state of destitution and humiliation.
value.literal: Then he repeatedly rebuked him: 'With your talents and abilities, you've brought yourself to this state of destitution and humiliation.

value.zh: 吾寧不能言而富貴子，子不足收也。」
value.en: I could easily speak on your behalf and make you wealthy and honored, but you are not worth saving."
value.literal: I could speak on your behalf and make you wealthy and honored, but you're not worth saving.'

value.zh: 謝去之。
value.en: He sent him away.
value.literal: He sent him away.

value.zh: 張儀之來也，自以為故人，求益，反見辱，怒，念諸侯莫可事，獨秦能苦趙，乃遂入秦。
value.en: Zhang Yi had come expecting to be treated as an old friend and receive assistance. Instead, he was humiliated. Angry, he realized that no other lord would employ him—only Qin could challenge Zhao. So he entered Qin.
value.literal: Zhang Yi had come expecting to be treated as an old friend and receive assistance. Instead he was humiliated. Angry, he realized no other lord would take him in—only Qin could challenge Zhao. So he went to Qin.

value.zh: 蘇秦已而告其舍人曰：「張儀，天下賢士，吾殆弗如也。
value.en: Later, Su Qin told his attendants, "Zhang Yi is the most talented man in the world. I am no match for him.
value.literal: Later, Su Qin told his attendants: 'Zhang Yi is the most talented man in the world. I am no match for him.

value.zh: 今吾幸先用，而能用秦柄者，獨張儀可耳。
value.en: Fortunately, I was employed first. The only one who can wield Qin's power is Zhang Yi alone.
value.literal: Fortunately, I was employed first. The only one who can wield Qin's power is Zhang Yi.

value.zh: 然貧，無因以進。
value.en: But Zhang Yi was poor and had no route by which to advance.
value.literal: But he is poor and has no means to advance himself.

value.zh: 吾恐其樂小利而不遂，故召辱之，以激其意。
value.en: I feared that he might be satisfied with petty gains and fail to accomplish anything great, so I summoned him here and humiliated him in order to rouse his ambition.
value.literal: I feared he might be content with small gains and not achieve great things, so I summoned and humiliated him to stir his ambition.

value.zh: 子為我陰奉之。」
value.en: Secretly support him for me."
value.literal: Secretly support him for me.'

value.zh: 乃言趙王，發金幣車馬，使人微隨張儀，與同宿舍，稍稍近就之，奉以車馬金錢，所欲用，為取給，而弗告。
value.en: He spoke to the King of Zhao, who provided gold, coins, chariots, and horses. Su Qin sent people to secretly follow Zhang Yi, share his lodging with him, gradually draw close to him, and provide him with chariots, horses, gold, and money—whatever he needed was supplied, without revealing who was behind it.
value.literal: He spoke to the King of Zhao, who provided gold, coins, chariots, and horses. Su Qin sent people to secretly follow Zhang Yi, share his lodging, gradually get close to him, and provide him with chariots, horses, gold, and money—whatever he needed, without telling him who was behind it.

value.zh: 張儀遂得以見秦惠王。
value.en: In this way, Zhang Yi gained an audience with King Hui of Qin.
value.literal: Thus, Zhang Yi was able to gain an audience with King Hui of Qin.

value.zh: 惠王以為客卿，與謀伐諸侯。
value.en: King Hui made him a guest minister and discussed plans with him for attacking the other feudal lords.
value.literal: King Hui appointed him as a guest minister and consulted with him on attacking the other feudal lords.

value.zh: 蘇秦之舍人乃辭去。
value.en: Su Qin's attendants then departed.
value.literal: Su Qin's attendants then took their leave.

value.zh: 張儀曰：「賴子得顯，方且報德，何故去也？」
value.en: Zhang Yi said, "Thanks to you, I have achieved prominence. I was just about to repay your kindness—why are you leaving?"
value.literal: Zhang Yi said, 'Thanks to you I have become prominent. I was just about to repay your kindness—why are you leaving?'

value.zh: 舍人曰：「臣非知君，知君乃蘇君。
value.en: The attendant said, "I do not know you; I know only Su Qin.
value.literal: The attendant said, 'I don't know you— I know Su Qin.

value.zh: 蘇君憂秦伐趙敗從約，以為非君莫能得秦柄，故感怒君，使臣陰奉給君資，盡蘇君之計謀。
value.en: Su Qin worried that Qin would attack Zhao and break the alliances. He believed that no one but you could control Qin's power, so he provoked you with anger and had me secretly support and provide for you, carrying out all of Su Qin's plans.
value.literal: Su Qin worried that Qin would attack Zhao and break the alliances. He believed no one but you could control Qin's power, so he provoked you with anger and had me secretly support and provide for you, carrying out all of Su Qin's plans.

value.zh: 今君已用，請歸報。」
value.en: Now that you are employed, let me return and report."
value.literal: Now that you are employed, let me return and report.'

value.zh: 張儀曰：「嗟乎，此在吾術中而不悟，吾不及蘇君明矣！
value.en: Zhang Yi said, "Alas, this was within my calculations, but I did not realize it. I am not as perceptive as Su Qin!
value.literal: Zhang Yi said, 'Alas, this was within my calculations but I didn't realize it. I am not as perceptive as Su Qin!

value.zh: 吾又新用，安能謀趙乎？
value.en: I have just been appointed—how could I possibly plot against Zhao?
value.literal: I have just been appointed—how can I plot against Zhao?

value.zh: 為吾謝蘇君，蘇君之時，儀何敢言。
value.en: Please apologize to Lord Su on my behalf. While Lord Su lives, how could I dare speak of such plans?
value.literal: Please convey my apologies to Su Qin. As long as Su Qin lives, how would I dare speak of such matters?

value.zh: 且蘇君在，儀寧渠能乎！」
value.en: As long as Su Qin lives, how could I possibly rival him!"
value.literal: As long as Su Qin lives, how could I possibly rival him!'

value.zh: 張儀既相秦，為文檄告楚相曰：「始吾從若飲，我不盜而璧，若笞我。
value.en: Once Zhang Yi became prime minister of Qin, he sent a formal declaration to the prime minister of Chu: "When I drank with you, I did not steal your jade disc, yet you had me beaten.
value.literal: Once Zhang Yi became prime minister of Qin, he sent a formal declaration to the prime minister of Chu: 'When I drank with you, I didn't steal your jade disc, yet you had me beaten.

value.zh: 若善守汝國，我顧且盜而城！」
value.en: If you guard your state well, I might just steal your cities instead!"
value.literal: If you guard your state well, I might just steal your cities instead!'

value.zh: 苴蜀相攻擊，各來告急於秦。
value.en: Ju and Shu attacked one another, and each came urgently to Qin requesting aid.
value.literal: The rulers of Shu and Ba attacked each other and both sent urgent appeals to Qin for assistance.

value.zh: 秦惠王欲發兵以伐蜀，以為道險狹難至，而韓又來侵秦，秦惠王欲先伐韓，後伐蜀，恐不利，欲先伐蜀，恐韓襲秦之敝。
value.en: King Hui of Qin wanted to send troops against Shu, but considered the roads too dangerous and narrow to reach it easily. At the same time, Han had come to invade Qin. King Hui wanted to attack Han first and Shu afterward, but feared this would not be advantageous; he wanted to attack Shu first, but feared Han would strike Qin while it was exhausted.
value.literal: King Hui of Qin wanted to send troops to attack Shu, but the roads were dangerous and narrow, making them difficult to traverse. Meanwhile, Han was invading Qin. King Hui wanted to attack Han first, then Shu, but feared it would be disadvantageous. He wanted to attack Shu first, but worried that Han would attack Qin while it was weakened.

value.zh: 猶豫未能決。
value.en: He wavered and could not make up his mind.
value.literal: He hesitated and couldn't decide.

value.zh: 司馬錯與張儀爭論於惠王之前，司馬錯欲伐蜀，張儀曰：「不如伐韓。」
value.en: Sima Cuo and Zhang Yi debated before King Hui. Sima Cuo wanted to attack Shu; Zhang Yi said, "Better to attack Han."
value.literal: Sima Cuo and Zhang Yi debated before King Hui. Sima Cuo wanted to attack Shu; Zhang Yi said, 'Better to attack Han.'

value.zh: 王曰：「請聞其說。」
value.en: The king said, "Let me hear your reasoning."
value.literal: The king said, 'Let me hear your reasoning.'

value.zh: 儀曰：「親魏善楚，下兵三川，塞什谷之口，當屯留之道，魏絕南陽，楚臨南鄭，秦攻新城、宜陽，以臨二周之郊，誅周王之罪，侵楚、魏之地。
value.en: Zhang Yi said, "Ally with Wei and befriend Chu. Send troops down to Sanchuan, block the Shigu pass, and occupy the Tunliu road. Cut off Nanyang from Wei, and have Chu threaten Nandun. Qin should attack Xincheng and Yiyang to approach the suburbs of the two Zhous. Punish the Zhou king's crimes, and invade Chu and Wei territory.
value.literal: Zhang Yi said: 'Ally with Wei and befriend Chu. Send troops down to Sanchuan, block the Shigu pass, occupy the Tunliu road. Cut off Nanyang from Wei, have Chu threaten Nandun. Qin attacks Xincheng and Yiyang to approach the suburbs of the two Zhous. Punish the Zhou king's crimes, invade Chu and Wei territory.

value.zh: 周自知不能救，九鼎寶器必出。
value.en: Zhou, knowing it cannot save itself, will be forced to surrender the Nine Tripods and its precious vessels.
value.literal: Zhou will realize it cannot save itself and will inevitably surrender the Nine Tripods and precious vessels.

value.zh: 據九鼎，案圖籍，挾天子以令於天下，天下莫敢不聽，此王業也。
value.en: Seize the Nine Tripods, control the maps and registers, and hold the Son of Heaven hostage to command the world; none would dare disobey. This is the work of a true king.
value.literal: Seize the Nine Tripods, control the maps and registers, hold the Son of Heaven hostage to command the world—none would dare disobey. This is the work of a true king.

value.zh: 今夫蜀，西僻之國而戎翟之倫也，敝兵勞眾不足以成名，得其地不足以為利。
value.en: As for Shu, it is a remote state in the west, of the same kind as the Rong and Di. To wear out the army and exhaust the people there would not win fame, and taking its territory would bring no real profit.
value.literal: Now Shu is a remote western land inhabited by barbarians. Wasting troops and exhausting the people there would not bring fame; gaining its territory would bring no benefit.

value.zh: 臣聞爭名者於朝，爭利者於市。
value.en: I have heard that men contend for reputation at court, and contend for profit in the marketplace.
value.literal: I have heard that those who compete for fame do so at court; those who compete for profit do so in the marketplace.

value.zh: 今三川、周室，天下之朝市也，而王不爭焉，顧爭於戎翟，去王業遠矣。」
value.en: Now Sanchuan and Zhou are the court and marketplace of the world. Yet Your Majesty does not compete there, instead competing with barbarians; that is far from true kingship."
value.literal: Now Sanchuan and Zhou are the court and marketplace of the world. Yet Your Majesty does not compete there, instead competing with barbarians—that is far from true kingship.'

value.zh: 秦惠王十年，使公子華與張儀圍蒲陽，降之。
value.en: In the tenth year of King Hui's reign, he dispatched Prince Hua and Zhang Yi to encircle Puyang, which yielded to them.
value.literal: In the tenth year of King Hui's reign, he sent Prince Hua and Zhang Yi to besiege Puyang, which surrendered.

value.zh: 儀因言秦復與魏，而使公子繇質於魏。
value.en: Zhang Yi then urged that Qin renew relations with Wei and send Prince You as hostage to Wei.
value.literal: Zhang Yi then proposed that Qin reconcile with Wei and send Prince You as hostage to Wei.

value.zh: 儀因說魏王曰：「秦王之遇魏甚厚，魏不可以無禮。」
value.en: Zhang Yi then addressed the King of Wei: "The King of Qin deals with Wei most generously. Wei cannot afford to be ungracious."
value.literal: Zhang Yi then persuaded the King of Wei: 'The King of Qin treats Wei very generously. Wei cannot be discourteous.'

value.zh: 魏因入上郡、少梁，謝秦惠王。
value.en: Wei accordingly offered up Shangdun and Shaoliang as thanks to King Hui of Qin.
value.literal: Wei therefore ceded Shangdun and Shaoliang to thank King Hui of Qin.

value.zh: 惠王乃以張儀為相，更名少梁曰夏陽。
value.en: King Hui therefore installed Zhang Yi as prime minister and rechristened Shaoliang as Xiayang.
value.literal: King Hui then appointed Zhang Yi as prime minister and renamed Shaoliang to Xiayang.

value.zh: 儀相秦四歲，立惠王為王。
value.en: Zhang Yi served as Qin's prime minister for four years and helped establish King Hui as king.
value.literal: Zhang Yi served as Qin prime minister four years, established King Hui as king.

value.zh: 居一歲，為秦將，取陜。
value.en: A year later, he commanded Qin's armies and captured Xie.
value.literal: After one year, he served as Qin's general and took Xie.

value.zh: 筑上郡塞。
value.en: He constructed defensive barriers in Shangdun.
value.literal: He built fortifications at Shangdun.

value.zh: 其後二年，使與齊、楚之相會齧桑。
value.en: Two years afterward, he met with the prime ministers of Qi and Chu at Yaosang.
value.literal: Two years later, he met with the prime ministers of Qi and Chu at Yaosang.

value.zh: 東還而免相，相魏以為秦，欲令魏先事秦而諸侯效之。
value.en: Upon returning east, he was relieved of his premiership. He became prime minister of Wei in Qin's service, intending for Wei to submit to Qin first so that other lords would follow suit.
value.literal: On his return east, he was dismissed as prime minister. He became prime minister of Wei to serve Qin, hoping Wei would submit to Qin first so other lords would follow.

value.zh: 魏王不肯聽儀。
value.en: The King of Wei would not heed Zhang Yi.
value.literal: The King of Wei refused to listen to Zhang Yi.

value.zh: 秦王怒，伐取魏之曲沃、平周，復陰厚張儀益甚。
value.en: The King of Qin grew furious and seized Wei's Quwo and Pingzhou. He covertly redoubled his patronage of Zhang Yi.
value.literal: The King of Qin was angry and attacked Wei's Quwo and Pingzhou. He secretly increased his support for Zhang Yi even more.

value.zh: 張儀慚，無以歸報。
value.en: Zhang Yi burned with shame, having no accomplishments to report.
